status: frozen 2026-10-13: final settings of the cross-city model (user decision); any change is sp_chicago_model_v4
supersedes: sp_chicago_model_v2 as the primary settings; v2 (hybrid, equal weights) and v1 stay unchanged and reproducible as published comparisons
decision: User, 13 October 2026, after reviewing scaling, runs, PCA distance, weights and correlations (MODEL_REPORT §12): compare every column by its position within its own city (all-relative), on the full calibrated distance, with family weights that favour land use and activity mix. M3 (long-tailed, carries about 3x its weight) and M7 (part of the grain cluster) leave the model; B1 returns at 0.10; U2 is halved to 0.05 because it duplicates U6 intensity (Spearman 0.83).
question: Which Chicago Community Area plays the role in Chicago that Brás plays in São Paulo: a non-residential working district with a similar activity mix, read relative to each city.
families: the 12 families of analysis/config/chicago_model_v1.json (definitions, tables and SHA-256), São Paulo rows from the same tables; family_columns overrides a family's columns (same as v2)
missing: U1 (all four shares) under 10% classified occupied land: Marsilac, Parelheiros, O'Hare; available-case distance (J-8)

settings.scaling_note: every column standardized within its own city (z-score, population SD, capped at +-3); U6 composition uses the city-centred log-ratios
settings.distance_note: the full calibrated distance (R1 geometry), not the PCA-truncated one
settings.family_weights_note: sum to 1; weights are renormalized over the families both units have (J-8); U6 = 1/2 intensity + 1/2 Aitchison composition
settings.column_weights_note: empty = every column weighs 1 inside its family (U1: four shares, 1/4 of U1 each; M4: two columns)

model.calibration: median positive pairwise value over all 14,878 pairs, per block
model.robustness: 500 weight draws around the v3 weights (seed 20261006, x U(0.5,1.5), 80% stability); named alternatives in comparison_v3.csv
model.implementation: analysis/scripts/sp_chicago_model_v3.py (reuses sp_chicago_model.py and chicago_model.py); report docs/harmonization/MODEL_REPORT.md §12
